records.issue_text: [BUG] `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)` is not a valid Java call — `picocli` is a package name (only `import picocli.CommandLine;` is present), so this is a compile error; there is no static `exit` accessor reachable via a bare package identifier, and picocli exposes no such member on `CommandLine` anyway. The quarkus runtime module fails to compile, breaking the whole build; the feature-disabled guard never ships and the documented exit-code-4 behavior cannot exist.
records.rationale: In both `UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run()` and `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()` the diff adds `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED);`. The call should likely reference `CommandLine` (if such a static method exists) or otherwise return/propagate an exit code via the command framework.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The docs promise 'the {project_name} Operator will fail' when rolling-updates is disabled, but this diff contains zero operator-side enforcement code — no check of Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ROLLING_UPDATES) or equivalent in any operator source file — so the documented failure behavior is not implemented by the changes shown. An operator user who sets spec.update.strategy without enabling the feature gets whatever the operator's default/ungated behavior is (likely a silent successful reconcile or an unrelated error), not the documented hard failure; the acceptance criterion stated in the shipped documentation cannot be met by the code in this PR.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The rolling-updates feature must be baked into the server image at build time (--features=rolling-updates on kc.sh build) for the update-compatibility commands to work, coupling the operator's upgrade path to a custom image build step rather than runtime configuration. Operators running the stock keycloak image (or any image built without the flag) get a hard failure of the update-compatibility tooling and, per the new CAUTION in advanced-configuration.adoc, the Operator itself; the failure surfaces only at upgrade time, not at deployment time, so an operator who enables spec.update.strategy=Recreate without rebuilding their image discovers the breakage during an actual upgrade attempt. The diff contains no runtime feature-flag path (env var / start argument) for the operator's own invocation of these commands, making the Dockerfile the only integration point.
